enonce: Where are Tom and his family?
texte:
Dear Lucy,
We are in Brighton! The weather is sunny, but the sea is cold. Yesterday we visited an old castle. It was great! I miss you.
See you soon,
Tom
reponses: Tom and his family are in Brighton.
explication: Tom starts his postcard with 'We are in Brighton!'. Answer with a full sentence: Tom and his family are in Brighton.

enonce: What did Tom and his family do yesterday?
texte:
Dear Lucy,
We are in Brighton! The weather is sunny, but the sea is cold. Yesterday we visited an old castle. It was great! I miss you.
See you soon,
Tom
reponses: Tom and his family visited an old castle.
Yesterday they visited an old castle.
Yesterday, they visited an old castle.
They visited an old castle yesterday.
explication: Read the sentence with 'Yesterday' in the postcard: 'Yesterday we visited an old castle.' In your answer, 'we' becomes 'they'.

enonce: Why does Chloe feel happy again at the end?
texte:
Hi Amy,
Today was a bad day. I forgot my homework at home, so Mrs Brown was angry. Then I lost my pencil case. At lunch I felt sad, but my friend Ali shared his sandwich with me. Now I feel happy again.
Love,
Chloe
reponses: She feels happy again because Ali shared his sandwich with her.
Chloe feels happy again because Ali shared his sandwich with her.
She feels happy because Ali shared his sandwich with her.
Chloe feels happy because Ali shared his sandwich with her.
She is happy again because Ali shared his sandwich with her.
explication: Chloe felt sad at lunch, then her friend Ali shared his sandwich with her. Use 'because' to give the reason.

enonce: What did Chloe forget to bring to school?
texte:
Hi Amy,
Today was a bad day. I forgot my homework at home, so Mrs Brown was angry. Then I lost my pencil case. At lunch I felt sad, but my friend Ali shared his sandwich with me. Now I feel happy again.
Love,
Chloe
reponses: She forgot her homework at home.
Chloe forgot her homework at home.
explication: Chloe writes: 'I forgot my homework at home.' In your answer, 'I' becomes 'she' and 'my' becomes 'her'.
astuce: Read the first two lines of the text again, slowly.

enonce: What number comes after ten?
explication: After ten comes eleven. You can write it as a word or a number.
astuce: Count on your fingers from ten.

enonce: Your mum's brother is your ___.
explication: Your mum's brother (or your dad's brother) is your uncle. A cousin is the child of your uncle or aunt.

enonce: Your friend says 'Thank you!' What do you say?
explication: When someone thanks you, you can answer 'You're welcome.'

enonce: I stayed at home ___ I was ill.
explication: 'Because' gives the reason. Why did I stay at home? Because I was ill.

enonce: Which food is healthy?
explication: An apple is a fruit. Fruit is good for your body.

enonce: Complete the rhyme: Hickory, dickory, dock. The mouse ran up the ___.
explication: 'Clock' rhymes with 'dock'. Rhyming words often end with the same sound.

enonce: Match each sign to what it means.
paires: The way out of the building
explication: Signs tell us quickly what to do or what to avoid. Read the words on each sign and find the sentence that explains it. For example, 'Exit' means the door you use to leave.

enonce: Put the school days in order, from Monday to Friday.
explication: The school week starts on Monday and finishes on Friday. The days always come in this same order, so the week goes Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday.

enonce: Match each word to its meaning.
paires: a person who looks after your teeth
a shop where you buy medicine
a person who helps sick people
a person who makes bread and cakes
explication: Some words name people or places. A dentist checks your teeth, and a chemist sells medicine. Learn each word with its meaning, not just its spelling.

enonce: Match each question or request to the best answer.
paires: Can I have a biscuit, please?
explication: In a short conversation, each question or request has a natural reply. 'Here you are' is what we say when we give something to someone. 'That's OK' is a kind answer to an apology.

enonce: Put these numbers in order, from the smallest to the biggest.
explication: Numbers ending in -teen are between 13 and 19: thirteen is 13. Numbers ending in -ty are tens: twenty is 20, thirty is 30. So the order is 12, 13, 20, 30, 44. Be careful not to mix up thirteen (13) and thirty (30)!

enonce: Put the sentences in the order they happen in the story.
elements: Sam runs to the bus stop.
Sam catches the bus to school.
Sam arrives at school just in time.
explication: Sam must wake up before he can run out of the house. He can only catch the bus after he reaches the bus stop, and he arrives at school at the end.

enonce: The word 'seven' has five letters.
explication: Vrai. S-E-V-E-N has five letters: s, e, v, e, n.

enonce: The word 'eight' has four letters.
explication: Faux. E-I-G-H-T has five letters: e, i, g, h, t.
astuce: Write the word on paper and count the letters one by one.

enonce: You can make green by mixing red and blue.
explication: Faux. Red and blue make purple. Green is made by mixing blue and yellow.

enonce: A kitten is a young cat.
explication: Vrai. A kitten is a baby cat, and a puppy is a baby dog.

enonce: A frog keeps its tail when it becomes an adult.
explication: Faux. A tadpole has a tail, but an adult frog does not.

enonce: A head teacher is the person in charge of a school.
explication: Vrai. The head teacher leads the whole school and its staff.

enonce: A hobby is a job you do to earn money.
explication: Faux. A hobby is something you do for fun in your free time, such as painting or swimming.

enonce: In the story of Cinderella, a fairy godmother helps her.
explication: Vrai. The fairy godmother magically helps Cinderella go to the ball.

enonce: Your lungs help you to hear.
explication: Faux. Your ears help you to hear. Your lungs help you to breathe.

enonce: Milk comes from cows.
explication: Vrai. Farmers milk cows, and we can drink the milk or make cheese and yoghurt with it.

enonce: Honey is made by spiders.
explication: Faux. Honey is made by bees from the nectar of flowers.

enonce: 'Nervous' means 'calm'.
explication: Faux. 'Nervous' means worried or a bit scared. 'Calm' means relaxed and quiet.

enonce: Mia is sniffling and her nose is red, so she probably has a cold.
explication: Vrai. Sniffling and a red nose are signs that someone has a cold.

enonce: Plants need water and sunlight to grow.
explication: Vrai. Plants need water, sunlight and air to grow and stay healthy.

enonce: The word 'actually' means 'now' in English.
explication: Faux. 'Actually' means 'in fact' or 'really'. 'Now' is a different word.

enonce: 'Quarter past six' means 6:15.
explication: Vrai. A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes, so a quarter past six is 6:15.

enonce: 'Quarter to six' means 6:15.
explication: Faux. 'Quarter to six' means 5:45, because it is a quarter of an hour before six.
astuce: Draw a clock face and count the minutes from the top.

enonce: After 'he', 'she' and 'it', the verb usually ends in -s.
explication: Vrai. For example: 'She likes football' and 'It runs fast'.

enonce: The plural of 'child' is 'childs'.
explication: Faux. The plural of 'child' is 'children'. It is an irregular plural.

enonce: We use 'first', 'then' and 'finally' to show the order of events.
explication: Vrai. These words link short sentences into a clear sequence: First, I woke up. Then, I had breakfast. Finally, I went to school.
